back: The bacterium *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*, usually in the lungs.
In droplets from the coughs and sneezes of a person with active TB, breathed in by others; worst in crowded, poorly ventilated places.
A cough lasting more than two weeks, night sweats, fever, chest pain and weight loss.

front: Why does HIV make active TB more likely?
back: HIV destroys lymphocytes, so the immune system can no longer keep latent TB bacteria inactive.
Several antibiotics taken every day for about six months; the whole course must be completed.
notes: Stopping early can lead to drug-resistant TB.

back: BCG vaccine at birth, early treatment, testing contacts, good ventilation, covering coughs and pasteurised milk.
In food and water contaminated with the faeces or urine of an infected person or a carrier.
A person with no symptoms who still passes the bacteria in their faeces and can infect others.
A long-lasting high fever, headache, weakness, abdominal pain, loss of appetite, constipation or diarrhoea.
Safe water, sanitation, handwashing with soap, food hygiene, treating carriers and vaccines for people at risk.
